title: Model Ecosystem Convergence Study — Rapid Threat Lateralization
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Objective: produce a compact, actionable report and dataset that identifies short-to-medium term convergence risks across model suppliers and quantifies where feature parity or availability shifts could materially affect Redwood customers. This ticket scopes a rapid study (3-week sprint) to lateralize threats (where multiple suppliers converge on the same capability set), map friction points (latency, token economics, API deltas), and create a prioritized operational response ladder (detection, mitigation, fallback).

Approach: 1) Build a lightweight survey matrix capturing: latency profiles, embedding/semantic drift risk, feature gaps (function calling, structured outputs, tool-calling compatibility), pricing elasticity and quantization readiness. 2) Run synthetic microbenchmarks (chat generation, embeddings, short-context reranking) across a representative set of open and hosted models using existing evaluation harness. 3) Combine live market telemetry (observability signals, usage telemetry anonymized) with procurement/availability alerts to estimate substitution cost curves. 4) Produce two artifacts: a concise playbook for SRE/Platform on automatic fallback thresholds and a model-convergence heatmap for GTM/product prioritization.

Scope boundaries: focus on models and vendors that are likely to be used by mid-market SaaS customers (latency sensitive and cost-sensitive use cases). Exclude purely academic or research-only experimental checkpoints unless they demonstrate an immediate parity threat.

Success criteria: deliver an evidence-backed ranking of top-10 convergence risks, recommended automatic fallback thresholds (token-cost, p50/p95 latency delta), and a first-pass alerting rule set to integrate into Console incident operations.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Heatmap PDF + CSV of supplier capability overlap and friction scores; 2) Synthetic microbenchmark results uploaded to shared drive with reproducible runbook; 3) Draft fallback threshold rules and three example alert rules for Console; 4) Presentation (<=12 slides) and an exec summary that product and SRE sign off on.
